candidates.label: Select active, retired, and removed
candidates.ownerGate: GON-OQ-001 CyberAlchemy Lab ontology lifecycle owner gate
evidence: CAL-GON-D019 defines lifecycle as whether a subject exists for use at a selected cursor and separates it from candidate status, maturity, promotion, projection, and authority posture
Creation is represented by the first accepted semantic event producing active state; no stored subject exists before that event
The closed values are active, retired, and removed; removed is a terminal semantic tombstone whose event history remains canonical
Allowed transitions are absent-to-active, active-to-retired, retired-to-active, active-to-removed, and retired-to-removed; removed has no successor transition
Only active nodes can satisfy active relation endpoint integrity; retired and removed subjects remain historically addressable but are excluded from the active ontology cut

This option is bound to definition-pack.json@sha256:9128208f453869ccb96c381d09a8df0cdd3274a5c039751a9519ac0746af825d and GONDEF decision.json@sha256:62496018fc321a6193fb73d079bd100d4595811b3c96564f8ecca7e375b9a01c

candidates.label: Select created, active, retired, and removed
candidates.ownerGate: GON-OQ-001 CyberAlchemy Lab ontology lifecycle owner gate
evidence: The closed values are created, active, retired, and removed; created means the subject identity exists in semantic history but is not eligible for ontology use or active relation endpoints
Allowed transitions are absent-to-created, created-to-active, created-to-removed, active-to-retired, retired-to-active, active-to-removed, and retired-to-removed; removed has no successor transition
This option preserves a pre-active semantic interval when a use case must address a newly created identity before it becomes usable
The created state must remain independent of review-candidate, evidence confidence, commitment confidence, promotion, and authority to avoid collapsing semantic lifecycle into governance workflow

This option is bound to definition-pack.json@sha256:9128208f453869ccb96c381d09a8df0cdd3274a5c039751a9519ac0746af825d and GONDEF decision.json@sha256:62496018fc321a6193fb73d079bd100d4595811b3c96564f8ecca7e375b9a01c

The OntologyLifecycleState definition would return to the definition owner before any executable schema work; the other 22 selected definitions remain bound unless a later exact amendment changes them

candidates.label: Store absent as a lifecycle value
candidates.ownerGate: GON-OQ-001 CyberAlchemy Lab ontology lifecycle owner gate
evidence: The selected architecture has one semantic event stream per identity-bearing subject and calculates lifecycle from that stream
rejectionReasons: A stored absent state presupposes the subject and stream whose absence it claims; absence belongs to projection lookup, not a subject event payload

candidates.label: Select only active and removed
candidates.ownerGate: GON-OQ-001 CyberAlchemy Lab ontology lifecycle owner gate
evidence: GON-OQ-001 explicitly requires the closed vocabulary to represent retirement independently of removal
rejectionReasons: The two-value set cannot represent retirement without moving it into governance state or collapsing it into removal
